question.problem: The $8$ members of a club are asked to elect $4$ officials: a president, a vice-president, a secretary, and a treasurer. How many different ways of electing the officials are possible?
question.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $8$ members to choose from, so $n=8.$ We want to select $4$ of those members to be officials, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different $4$-member official teams is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{8}{P}_{4} & =\frac{8!}{(8-4)!} \\  & =\frac{8!}{4!} \\  & =\frac{8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot 5\cdot \cancel{4!}}{\cancel{4!}} \\  & =8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot 5 \\  & =1\,680.\end{aligned}
$$
